### 5. Chapter Lens Relevance Assessment

| Chapter | Relevance | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1B (Nuclear/Global Risk)** | **Low** | Biography is political career narrative; no direct nuclear doctrine, command-and-control, arms-control agreements, or proliferation policy. The " Guardia Nacional" is a domestic security instrument, not nuclear. |
| **2B (International Peace/Aggression)** | **Medium** | Trump border disputes (U0007, U0057–U0058, U0063–U0064), 2006 electoral confrontation and "legítimo" parallel government (U0036–U0038), opposition to Peña Nieto energy reforms (U0053–U0054). No direct armed conflict authorization. |
| **3B (Domestic Safety)** | **Medium** | Security policy promises (Guardia Nacional, addressing causes of violence), criminal violence statistics (200,000 dead since 2006), but biography does not assess implementation quality. |
| **4B (Political Freedom)** | **High** | Core document theme — electoral fraud allegations (2006, 2012), self-proclaimed "presidente legítimo," 2005 desafuero, PRD/MORENA institutional relationships, media access, term limits, democratic resilience. |
| **5B (Economic Wellbeing)** | **Medium** | Platform promises on growth (6%), jobs, minimum wages, austerity, FOBAPROA opposition, energy policy; no implementation evidence in this biography. |
| **6B (Social Wellbeing)** | **Medium** | Social programs promised (adult pensions, youth employment, food sovereignty); DF social management record (2000–2005); implementation not assessed here. |
| **7B (Integrity)** | **High** | Videoescándalo (U0021–U0023) — corruption of close collaborators (Bejarano, Ponce, Ímaz), late/timid response; false fraud claims (2006, 2012); FOBAPROA exposé; "no mentir, no robar, no traicionar" pledge. |
| **8B (Effectiveness)** | **Highest** | Biography is fundamentally a political trajectory narrative: stated programs (U0005–U0006, U0030–U0031, U0046–U0048, U0062–U0063), DF implementation record (U0019–U0020), appointment of capable people, coordination, crisis management (desafuero, 2006 election crisis), and period-end assessment (presidential victory as effectiveness signal). |

### 7. Source Limitations for Ruler-Quality Assessment

| Limitation | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Publication date gap** | Biography ends at ~August 2018; 2018–2024 presidential implementation not covered |
| **Genre bias** | Biography foregrounds political narrative, personality, and institutional context; policy implementation evidence is thin |
| **No independent verification** | Relies on subject's own published accounts; "victimization" framing prominent in 2006–2012 sections |
| **Limited quantitative data** | No structured indicator data; economic/social statistics referenced only as rhetorical context |
| **Missing 6B.9 / 6B.10** | Social institution durability — biography ends at inauguration, not end-of-period |
| **Political freedom lens gap** | While 4B themes are richly present, no systematic treatment of actual democratic-institutional quality during the target period |
